### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via os secret rewrap (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via os secret rewrap (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8d34c4404f951410083a6caebd6ad8003ea3423d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf1ed2590c214c19823b8faaf94aab52586e2efb` — the merge of head `00049e7be83628c9540f1bc3380d941a8e4c3873` into base `8d34c4404f951410083a6caebd6ad8003ea3423d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf1ed2590c214c19823b8faaf94aab52586e2efb && git checkout cf1ed2590c214c19823b8faaf94aab52586e2efb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8d34c4404f951410083a6caebd6ad8003ea3423d 00049e7be83628c9540f1bc3380d941a8e4c3873 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8d34c4404f951410083a6caebd6ad8003ea3423d && git merge --no-ff 00049e7be83628c9540f1bc3380d941a8e4c3873

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8d34c4404f951410083a6caebd6ad8003ea3423d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8d34c4404f951410083a6caebd6ad8003ea3423d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b15bd751db812bb43a40019fdee822bc77d71ec2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts, packages/cli/test/orphans-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/cli/src/commands/db/orphans.ts and packages/cli/src/commands/secret/orphans.ts (the `--yes` gate and `confirm()`), packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/** (every `isTTY` gate), packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts (its population walk), packages/cli/src/utils/sys-secret-rewrap.ts (`planSysSecretRewrap`, `refusal`, `attempts`), packages/cli/src/utils/one-shot-settings.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.guards.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts, the layout of packages/cli/src/commands/**, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .changeset/pre.json, .changeset/config.json, AGENTS.md (the changeset rule), content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx § `os secret rewrap`

Read on this head: the net diff against `main` at `3e8edf78c2d16738a7740bcd68e33158d96691a5` (3 files, +187/-51), card #36679 with its three comments (triage 7099072147, claim 7226704095, os-dev report 7227989647; no ruling among them), the PR body and its two comments, PR #36676 with its changeset and both contract-review records (7111408857, 7112313456), and the check-runs on this head: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. The skipped runs are the path-filtered UI and docs jobs and the opt-in jobs.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: no change. No flag, argument, value or `--json` key is added, removed or re-typed. `Clause-②: no` is right.
- Public surface, exit status: one narrowing. `os secret rewrap --apply`, without `--yes`, text face, `process.stdin.isTTY` falsy, with a plan of one or more attempts: exit `0` becomes exit `1`. The new branch sits inside the existing gate (`flags.apply`, a plan with attempts, and no `flags.yes`), after the `--json` branch and before `confirm()`. Declared `(narrowing)`: right.
- Public surface, printed line: on that path `Aborted — no row was opened or written.` (info) becomes `Confirmation required. Re-run with --yes to re-wrap. No row was opened or written.` (warning), each followed by the journal-mode note on a SQLite file. Right, and true: the branch exits before `executeSysSecretRewrap`, so no row is opened or written.
- The exit fires in that one case and no other. Each read in the tree:
  - a terminal answered `n`: `confirm()` returns false, `Aborted — …`, plain return, exit 0. Unchanged.
  - `--json` without `--yes`: `confirmation_required`, exit 1, the same bytes as on `main`. Unchanged.
  - a dry run (no `--apply`): the gate's first conjunct is false. Unchanged.
  - `--yes`: the gate is skipped whole. Unchanged.
  - `--apply` with zero attempts: the gate is skipped, no prompt. Unchanged.
  - stdin a pipe, a closed pipe or `/dev/null`: `isTTY` is undefined, so exit 1. On `main` each of these already refused (`confirm()` returned false before it read anything), so a piped `y` never confirmed; only the status moves.
  - CI detection: none. The test is `process.stdin.isTTY` alone, with no `CI` variable read. A job that allocates a pseudo-terminal is prompted, as on `main` and as in every sibling.
- The refusals that come before the gate (unreadable declared datasources, crypto provider, boot, union incomplete, no compare-and-set writer, no key) are untouched and still exit 1 first.
- `this.exit(1)` is thrown inside the `try` whose `catch` rethrows on `isExitSignal` and whose `finally` shuts the stack down, so the exit is not rewritten to `scan_failed` and the stack is closed.
- Against #36676, line for line: `db/orphans.ts` and `secret/orphans.ts` carry the same three steps in the same order (`--json` emits and returns; `!process.stdin.isTTY` warns and `this.exit(1)`; the prompt's decline prints `Aborted — …` and returns), with the same `confirm()` body. The three now behave identically at the gate. Two differences remain and both are the commands' own shape, not drift: rewrap's gate also tests `flags.apply` and a non-zero `plan.attempts` because its default mode is a dry run that reaches the same code, where the orphans commands return before the gate; and rewrap prints no "About to …" line before the refusal.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/cli': patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. No spec key, authorable value or stored shape moves. AGENTS.md on this head: "`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `.changeset/pre.json` is in pre mode (tag `next`), and `@objectstack/cli` is in the fixed group of `.changeset/config.json`, so the level is the group's and a `patch` entry raises nothing. This is the level #36676 shipped. `Check Changeset`: success.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: right, and present on both the PR body and the changeset. Title and changeset headline carry `!`. The banner carries FROM / TO / Unchanged / the fix for a script.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right. Nothing exists for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; the remedy is a flag on the caller's command line. `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint & Repo Gates`: success.
- The changeset prose against the code: the headline, FROM, TO, the terminal-`n` clause, the `--json` clause, the `--yes` clause, the script remedy and the closing sentence about the `os migrate` and orphans commands each hold. One clause is loose, see the nit in ④.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` § `os secret rewrap` left as is: accepted. The section lists `-y, --yes — skip the confirmation prompt` and states no exit status for an unconfirmed run, so nothing in it is falsified.
- `Skills-docs: none`: true. No file under `skills/` names `rewrap`.
- In-repo callers: none relies on the old status. Every `--apply` run of the command in tests passes `--yes` (`rewrap.guards.test.ts`, `rewrap.driver-contract.test.ts`, `schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts`), except the two that mean not to: the `--json` refusal case and the decline case, which sets a terminal. No workflow under `.github` and no script under `scripts/` runs the command.
- File surface against claim 7226704095: exactly the three claimed paths.
- Dogfood battery owed by the `(narrowing)` arm: the dev reports a full run at this head with no failure. That is the dev's reading, not re-run here. `Dogfood Regression Gate` on this head: success.
- SQL push-down: no new query, id materialisation or in-app join. The source hunk adds one branch on `process.stdin.isTTY`; the pin runs on fakes.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

- The narrowing takes no declared capability away. Nothing on `main` declares exit 0 for an unconfirmed `--apply`: the `--yes` flag text says it skips the prompt, the `--json` flag text says applying "requires --yes", and `cli.mdx` is silent on the status. The refusal was already real (nothing opened, nothing written); the status and the line now report it. What a script loses is reading a no-op as a key rotation, which is the defect the card names. Both remedies work on this head: `--yes` re-wraps, and dropping `--apply` gives the dry-run report.
- Tried to break it, and it held: (a) a non-interactive run cannot reach the prompt or the executor; (b) the exit signal is not swallowed; (c) the pin's text-face case cannot pass on some other exit 1, because the earlier refusals do not print `--yes` and the `--yes` control, on the same fixture and argv, exits 0 with exactly one write, which needs the real planner to attribute the row and the real local provider to open, re-seal and verify it; (d) the pin sets `process.stdin.isTTY` per run and restores it, and saves and restores the key environment; (e) the existing decline case in `rewrap.guards.test.ts` runs on a terminal, so it does not contradict the change.
- The rewrap row runs what the header says it runs. `secret-reference-union.js` is mocked to a seam that the fixture points back at the real function; `sys-secret-rewrap.js` (planner, executor) and `oneShotCrypto` are not mocked; the boot is replaced and the fixture drives the host crypto seam by hand. The ablation reading fits the code: without the new `this.exit(1)` a non-terminal run falls through to `confirm()`, which answers false, so the run prints `Aborted — …` and exits 0, and only the rewrap text-face case goes red. `Test Core` 10/10: success.
- Migrate's exclusion is justified: `migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts` owns `src/commands/migrate/**` with its own population, which includes the one member confirmed by `--backup-taken`, so a single `yes`-keyed population could not hold it.
- S1 (should-fix) — the population is derived, but over a walk that does not reach every command, so the claim the PR makes for it is not true. The roster equality is read off the classes' flags, which is right. The walk feeding it reads only modules exactly one directory below `src/commands`, and imports only a module whose source matches the text `yes: Flags.boolean`. On this head that reaches 47 of the 71 command modules outside `migrate`. The 21 top-level modules (`deploy.ts` among them, the one that already prompts) and the 3 under `plugin/trust/` are not read, and a flag spelled with a quoted key or taken from a shared flag set is not imported. A `--yes` added to any of those joins no population and no pin fails. The header ("every command outside `os migrate`", "the next such command fails here"), the PR body and the card's third done-when ("caught by construction") all state more than that. The #36676 record 7111408857 recorded this reach as a nit and folded its fix into this card; this PR widens the flag predicate and leaves the reach as it was, without naming it as a deviation. The sibling migrate pin already descends ("the walk descends"). No escaped command exists today, so product behaviour is not wrong; the pin's stated guarantee is. The fix is in the pin file: walk `src/commands` recursively minus `migrate`, top level included, as the migrate pin does. It moves the head and earns a delta review.
- nit — the changeset's Unchanged clause "a dry run, or an `--apply` run with nothing to re-wrap, exits `0` without asking" is unconditional where the code is not. A dry run with a row to open and no data key exits 1, and an `--apply` run whose reference union is incomplete exits 1 (`union_incomplete`) with zero attempts. Neither path is touched by this PR, so "unchanged" holds; "exits `0`" holds only for a run that is not otherwise refused. The PR body repeats it. Fixable on the prose face, or left as an accepted deviation; #36676 worded its clause the same way.
- nit — `cli.mdx` § `os secret rewrap` could state the refusal the way one `os migrate` entry on that page does ("without it, a run whose stdin is not a terminal (or `--json`) … exits `1`"). Nothing there is false. A follow-up for the three commands together, not this PR.

Scope — the narrowing is declared of the whole PR, never of a path: the floor is EVERY path of the diff outside the
  prose faces (`content/docs/**`, `.changeset/**`), plus every file those hunks make a claim about, read in the cited code.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below that floor; the record's `Scope:` line lists both. No path is the lane seat's remainder.

  the PR are not reviewed; the published spec and the cited code are READ to judge it, never reviewed.

   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38042/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — the narrowing itself, read against the published spec on `main`: does it take a
     declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real? A capability declared
     and not delivered is an implementation gap, implemented or retired, ⛔ never narrowed at the consumer.
     Read the spec and the cited code in the live tree, and try to break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `00049e7be83628c9540f1bc3380d941a8e4c3873`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts, packages/cli/test/orphans-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: the layout of packages/cli/src/commands/** (every module path, extension and default export), packages/cli/package.json (the `oclif.commands` pattern), packages/cli/src/commands/build.ts and compile.ts (an inherited flag set), packages/cli/src/utils/sys-secret-rewrap.ts (`refusal`, `attempts`), packages/cli/test/migrate-confirmation-exit.pin.test.ts

### ① Derived judgments

The one narrowing is the exit status `0` to `1` on the text face of `os secret rewrap --apply`, without `--yes`, with stdin not a terminal and a plan with attempts. ### ② Semver level

Unchanged and right: `'@objectstack/cli': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. One changeset sentence moved, see ④. `Check Changeset`: success on this head.

- Dev flag, the cli unit layer and the typecheck not re-run locally because no source moved: answered by the head's check-runs. `Test Core` 10/10, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are success.
- Dogfood battery: the dev reports a full run at this head with no failure. That is the dev's reading, not re-run here. `Dogfood Regression Gate`: success.

### ④ Design judgment
